description: Synthetic retrieval questions labeled against the saved public Chase Sapphire Reserve snapshot. expectedHeading is the section that answers the question, or null when the snapshot has no supporting passage and the app should abstain. Cases tagged "holdout" were written and frozen before the verified-retrieval design was built; they are report-only and never used to tune thresholds or prompts. The first holdout exposed a false answer from the model judge alone, so it is now a regression set; "holdout2" was written and frozen before the distinctive-word safeguard was built. Success rule fixed in advance: ship a verified-retrieval variant only with zero false answers and zero wrong passages on every split. holdout2 exposed a false answer from the strict cutoff itself ("travel" overlap at 0.713), so it also became a regression set; "holdout3" (including near-miss questions that reuse words like travel and lounge) was frozen before verification was extended to strict matches. "holdout4" was frozen after the comparative-selection variant was designed on the development split and before that variant was run on any holdout; it is the only split that can fairly judge it. Near-miss unsupported questions reuse words that appear in the source.
